children: is developing a screenless fitness tracker that could compete with devices from Whoop, Bloomberg News reported on Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter.
The device is still in an early development stage and Apple has not decided whether to release it, Bloomberg reported. If launched, it would not be expected before 2028.
Prototypes include a thin fabric band with a sensor-equipped module but no display, distinguishing the device from Apple's Apple Watch.
Bloomberg reported that Apple executive chairman Tim Cook and services chief Eddy Cue have taken an interest in the project.
Apple did not immediately respond to Seeking Alpha requests for comment.
Apple is a leading smartwatch maker, but companies such as Whoop and Garmin
have built products aimed at athletes and people seeking more specialized fitness tracking.
Garmin shares pared earlier gains to trade roughly flat following the report.

, which makes smart ring that provides consumers with a variety of fitness and personal information to aid them in their health and wellness goals, announced that it has launched its initial public offering of 50M shares of its common stock.
